title: Waves and photons
summary: Wavelength, frequency and the speed of light; why light comes in photons with E = hc/λ; and the difference between brighter and bluer.

diagrams.title: From wavelength to photon energy
diagrams.tryThis: Slide from violet (400 nm) to the infrared (1200 nm): the energy per photon halves and halves again, while the number of photons in 1 W goes up.

checks.prompt: What is the frequency of orange light with a wavelength of 600 nm (in vacuum)?
Silicon has a bandgap of 1.12 eV. What is the longest wavelength (in nm) a photon can have and still carry at least this energy?
Light passes from air into glass ($n$ = 1.5). Which quantity stays the same?

options.text: The frequency (and hence the photon energy)
options.feedback: Correct: the frequency is set by the source; speed and wavelength both drop by a factor n.
The wavelength shrinks to λ₀/n inside the glass.
Light slows to c/n = 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s in glass.
Frequency (and therefore photon energy hν) is unchanged.

hints: $\lambda = c/(n\nu)$: which quantity has no n in it?
The source decides how often the field oscillates.
solution: The frequency stays the same; the speed becomes c/n and the wavelength λ₀/n.
Because $E = h\nu$, photon energy is also unchanged in the glass.
